says: When the filter dialog is confirmed, the policy type is kept only if the person picked Policy (managed policies only) or Preference (non-managed only); Any adds no restriction on type.
When the filter dialog is confirmed, the current-state filter becomes Not Configured, Configured, Enabled or Disabled as picked; Any adds no restriction on state.
When the filter dialog is confirmed, the commented filter keeps only commented policies for Yes, only uncommented ones for No; Any adds no restriction on comments.

When the filter dialog is confirmed with 'Supported on' ticked, the filter keeps the ticked products plus the two matching options (at least one selected product supported; policies with missing or blank support). When it is not ticked, no product restriction applies and those options are dropped.

When the filter dialog opens or Reset is pressed with no product restriction, 'Supported on' is unticked, all products unticked, and both matching options ticked; Reset applies this to an empty filter.
When the filter dialog opens with an existing filter, its type, state, comment and product choices are shown as selected, and only the products it names are ticked.
The product list and its two matching options are usable only while 'Supported on' is ticked.
When a person ticks or unticks a product, every product beneath it takes the same tick; ticks set by the program itself do not spread.
Pressing Escape in the filter dialog closes it as cancelled and the filter is unchanged.

When an ID is typed in Find by ID, surrounding spaces are ignored and the ID is looked up in this order: category, product, support definition, then policy; the first kind found is the one selected and the others are cleared.
When the typed ID is not a category, product or support definition, text after the first '@' is cut off before the policy lookup, so 'ID@U' finds the same policy as 'ID'.
When a policy is found and the ID ends in '@U' it is selected for the User section, '@C' for the Computer section; with no suffix or any other suffix it is selected for both sections.
When the typed ID matches nothing, a not-found icon is shown, or a blank icon if the box is empty; no selection is made.
Pressing Go in Find by ID closes the dialog as accepted whether or not the typed ID matched; the caller receives whichever selection exists.
Pressing Escape in Find by ID closes it as cancelled.
Text changes in Find by ID are ignored until the dialog has been given a definitions workspace, and the starting single space is cleared when it first appears.
When Search is pressed in Find by Registry with both key and value boxes empty, nothing is searched and the person is told "Please enter search terms."

When the key text begins with HKLM\, HKCU\, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\ or HKEY_CURRENT_USER\ (any letter case), nothing is searched and the person is told "Policies' root keys are determined only by their section. Remove the root key from the search terms and try again."
A policy matches a registry search when at least one registry value it refers to satisfies every filled-in box; empty boxes impose nothing.
When a value name is entered, only values whose whole name matches it count, ignoring letter case; '*' and '?' act as wildcards.
When the key text holds '*' or '?', the whole key path must match it as a wildcard pattern, ignoring letter case.
When the key text holds a backslash and no wildcard, the key path must start with it, ignoring letter case.
When the key text has no backslash or wildcard, a key matches if any one folder name in its path equals it, ignoring letter case.
Pressing Escape in Find by Registry closes it as cancelled.
When Search is pressed in Find by Text with no text, nothing is searched and the person is told "Please enter search terms."

When none of In title, In description, In comment is ticked, nothing is searched and the person is told "At least one attribute must be searched. Check one of the boxes and try again." All three start ticked.

The search text is split on spaces into plain words, wildcard words (containing '*' or '?') and quoted phrases starting at a word that begins with a double quote and ending at a word that ends with one.
Before comparing, text and search terms are lowercased and the characters . , ' " ; / ! ( ) { } [ ] are removed, so matching ignores case and that punctuation.
A quoted phrase that is never closed is dropped, and the words after its opening quote are swallowed with it; a search left with no terms matches every policy that has the searched text.

A piece of text is a hit only when every plain word is a whole word in it, every wildcard word matches some word in it, and every quoted phrase appears as consecutive whole words; words are split on spaces and line breaks.
A policy matches when its title (if In title ticked) or its explanation (if In description ticked) is a hit.
A policy matches on comments (if In comment ticked) when any supplied comment source holds a comment for that policy that is a hit.
Pressing Escape in Find by Text closes it as cancelled.
When Search Results is opened with no search run since start or since the last clear, the person is told "No search has been run yet, so there are no results to display." and nothing opens.

When a search is started, previous results are cleared, progress is sized to the number of policies loaded, the Stop button is enabled and the status reads 'Starting search'; the new results replace the old.
Clearing the search (when definitions are opened, closed, acquired or the language changes) discards the results, so Search Results again reports that no search has run.
Find Next returns the result after the last one chosen, starting from the first if none was chosen; at the end of the list, or with no search, it returns nothing.
A search tests every loaded policy in turn; those the search function accepts are listed with title and category, added in batches every 20 policies checked.
When Stop is pressed or the dialog closes, the search ends at the next policy; hits found so far stay listed.

A finished search reports 'Finished searching: checked N policies, found M hits' and a stopped one 'Search canceled: checked N policies, found M hits'; Stop is then disabled and progress shows full. Mid-search it shows 'Searching: checked N policies so far, found M hits'.
When the dialog is closed during a search, no further results or status are written, and the label reads 'Search canceled'.
A search starts only when the dialog appears after a search request; reopening it instead reselects the last chosen result if it is still in the list.
Go, or double-clicking a result, with a result selected remembers it, returns it to the caller and closes as accepted; with nothing selected nothing happens.
Re-opening Search Results without a new search does not rerun it and clears the stop flags so it shows earlier results.
When a REG file is browsed and the prefix box is empty, the prefix is filled with the prefix guessed from the file.
When that guessed REG file holds default values, the person is warned "This REG file contains data for default values, which cannot be applied to all policy sources."
When the REG file cannot be read to guess the prefix, the person is told "An error occurred while trying to guess the prefix."
Only files ending .reg are offered when browsing for a REG file.
When Import is pressed with no REG file, nothing is imported and the person is told "Please specify a REG file to import."
When Import is pressed with no prefix, nothing is imported and the person is told "Please specify the prefix used to fully qualify paths in the REG file."

When the REG file is read with the prefix and applied to the policy source without error, the dialog closes as accepted; on any error the person is told "Failed to import the REG file." and the dialog stays open.
Pressing Escape in Import REG closes it as cancelled; opening it clears the file and prefix boxes.
Verify reads the text as an SPOL file: valid text reports "Validation successful, N policy settings found."; invalid text reports "SPOL validation failed: " and the reason. Nothing is applied.
Apply reads the text as an SPOL file: valid text is handed back as ready and the dialog closes as accepted; invalid text stays open with "The SPOL text is invalid: " and the reason.
Reset asks "Are you sure you want to reset the text box?"; only Yes replaces the text with the header "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line.
Pressing Escape in Import SPOL closes it as cancelled unless text in the box is selected; opening it clears any earlier result.

statement: Whether a typed ID in Find by ID must match letter case depends on how the definitions lookup tables compare text, which is not in these files.

assumed.why: The lookup tables are built elsewhere and their comparison setting is not shown here.
assumed.ifWrong: People might need exact letter case, or case might be ignored, when finding by ID.

evidence.shows: The ID is looked up directly in dictionaries with no case change.
